      "text": "Based on the provided lecture notes, here is the comprehensive Obsidian-ready markdown reconstruction. I have organized the disparate images into a logical academic structure, separating general mechanics, fluid dynamics, and rotational dynamics.\n\n***\n\n# Lecture: Mechanics, Hydrodynamics \u0026 Rotational Dynamics\n\n**Date:** [[2025-11-27]]\n**Location:** Slovenia\n**Tags:** #Physics #Mechanics #Hydrodynamics #RotationalDynamics #Obsidian\n\n---\n\n## 1. General Formulas \u0026 Identities Used\nBefore diving into specific problems, the following mathematical identities and physical principles were utilized throughout the lecture:\n\n### Trigonometry\n*   **Fundamental Identity:** $\\sin^2 \\alpha + \\cos^2 \\alpha \u003d 1$\n*   **Cosine Rule (implied in vector subtraction):** $c^2 \u003d a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \\cos \\gamma$\n*   **Transformation:** Used to decouple coupled equations in elastic collisions.\n\n### Physics Principles\n*   **Newton\u0027s Second Law (Impulse form):** $\\vec{F} \u003d \\frac{d\\vec{G}}{dt} \\implies \\int \\vec{F} dt \u003d \\Delta \\vec{G}$\n*   **Conservation of Angular Momentum:** $\\Gamma_{total} \u003d \\text{const}$ if $M_{ext} \u003d 0$.\n*   **Jet Force (Hydrodynamics):** $\\vec{F} \u003d \\Phi_m (\\vec{v}_{out} - \\vec{v}_{in})$ where $\\Phi_m \u003d \\rho S v$.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Linear Dynamics \u0026 Projectiles\n*(Based on Image 1)*\n\n### Problem Setup: Cylinder/Block Push\nA block of mass $m\u003d1 \\text{ kg}$ is pushed along a surface by a constant force $F\u003d500 \\text{ N}$ for a distance $\\Delta x$ (related to diameter $2R\u003d10 \\text{ cm}$). It then behaves as a horizontal projectile falling from height $H\u003d10 \\text{ m}$.\n\n**Objective:** Calculate the range (domet) $d$.\n\n### 2.1. Acceleration Phase\nWe assume a constant force acts on the mass. Using [[Work-Energy Theorem]] or Kinematics:\n$$ F \u003d m \\cdot a \\implies a \u003d \\frac{F}{m} $$\nVelocity after pushing distance $\\Delta x$:\n$$ v^2 \u003d v_0^2 + 2a \\Delta x $$\nAssuming starting from rest ($v_0\u003d0$) and $\\Delta x \\approx 2R$ (as per notes):\n$$ v \u003d \\sqrt{2 \\cdot \\frac{F}{m} \\cdot 2R} $$\n\n\u003e **Note to Self:** The notes define $\\Delta x \\le 2R$. The calculation assumes the force acts over the full diameter.\n\u003e *Calculation in notes:*\n\u003e $$ v \u003d \\sqrt{2 \\cdot \\frac{500}{1} \\cdot 0.1} \u003d \\sqrt{100} \u003d 10 \\text{ m/s} $$\n\u003e *Wait, notes show $\\sqrt{300^2 \\dots}$. This segment connects to the \"bullet\" problem later. Let\u0027s stick to the visual derivation of the projectile part.*\n\n### 2.2. Projectile Motion Phase\nOnce the object leaves the platform with horizontal velocity $v_x$, it falls height $H$.\nTime of flight $t$:\n$$ H \u003d \\frac{1}{2} g t^2 \\implies t \u003d \\sqrt{\\frac{2H}{g}} $$\nHorizontal range $d$:\n$$ d \u003d v_x \\cdot t \u003d v_x \\sqrt{\\frac{2H}{g}} $$\n\n### 2.3. Impulse \u0026 Average Force\nThe notes discuss the definition of external force as the time derivative of momentum ([[Impulse]]):\n$$ \\vec{F}_{zun} \u003d \\frac{d\\vec{G}}{dt} \\implies \\int \\vec{F} dt \u003d \\Delta \\vec{G} $$\n\n---\n\n## 3. Collisions in 2D\n*(Based on Image 2 and 3)*\n\n### Problem: Elastic/Inelastic Collision\nTwo bodies, masses $m_1$ and $m_2$, collide.\n*   **Initial State:** $m_1$ moves with $v_1$, $m_2$ is stationary ($v_2\u003d0$).\n*   **Final State:** They scatter at angles $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$.\n\n**Conservation of Momentum (Vectorial):**\n$$ m_1 \\vec{v}_1 \u003d m_1 \\vec{v}\u0027_1 + m_2 \\vec{v}\u0027_2 $$\n\n**Decomposition (x and y axes):**\n$$ X: \\quad m_1 v_1 \u003d m_1 v\u0027_1 \\cos \\alpha + m_2 v\u0027_2 \\cos \\beta $$\n$$ Y: \\quad 0 \u003d m_1 v\u0027_1 \\sin \\alpha - m_2 v\u0027_2 \\sin \\beta $$\n\n### Critical Analysis: Solving the System\nThe lecturer performed a derivation to relate the angles.\nFrom Y-direction:\n$$ v\u0027_1 \\sin \\alpha \u003d \\frac{m_2}{m_1} v\u0027_2 \\sin \\beta $$\nUsing the identity $\\sin^2 \\alpha + \\cos^2 \\alpha \u003d 1$, the notes derive a relationship between the cosine of the scattering angles, specifically resulting in:\n$$ \\cos \\alpha + 2 \\cos \\beta \u003d 2 $$\n*(This specific result implies specific mass ratios or velocities were plugged in, e.g., $v_2 \u003d 2v_1$).*\n\n---\n\n## 4. Hydrodynamics: Force of a Jet (Sila Curka)\n*(Based on Image 4 and 5)*\n\n### Concept: Jet Impact\nA fluid jet with velocity $v$ and cross-section $S$ hits a plate. The force exerted is due to the change in momentum flux.\n\n$$ \\vec{F}_{curka} \u003d \\Phi_m (\\vec{v}_{out} - \\vec{v}_{in}) $$\nWhere mass flow rate $\\Phi_m \u003d \\rho S v$.\n\n### Problem: Jet Hitting a Hinged Plate\nA plate of mass $M$ and length $L$ hangs vertically. A jet hits it, deflecting it by angle $\\phi$.\n\n**Equilibrium of Moments:**\nTorque due to Gravity \u003d Torque due to Jet\n$$ M_g \u003d M_{curka} $$\n$$ m g \\frac{L}{2} \\sin \\phi \u003d F_{curka} \\cdot r_{curka} \\cdot \\cos \\phi $$\n*(Note: The cosine term comes from the component of the jet force perpendicular to the plate).*\n\n**Resulting Equation from Notes:**\n$$ \\sin \\phi \u003d \\frac{4 \\rho S v^2 h}{mg L} $$\nSolving for $\\phi$:\n$$ \\phi \u003d \\arcsin \\left( \\frac{4 \\rho S v^2 h}{mg L} \\right) $$\n*Calculated result:* $\\phi \u003d 24.79^{\\circ}$.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Rotational Dynamics: The \"Salt on Disk\" Problem\n*(Based on Image 5 and 6)*\n\n### Problem Statement\nWe have a rotating disc. Above it hangs a bag of salt.\n*   **Initial State:** Disc (radius $R$, mass $M$) rotates with $\\omega_0$. Bag is stationary above.\n*   **Process:** Salt falls uniformly from a hole in the bag onto the disc at a radius $b$.\n*   **System:** Disc + Accumulating Salt.\n*   **Constraint:** After $t\u003d30$ seconds, the angular velocity drops to $\\omega(30) \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\omega_0$.\n\n**Objective:** Calculate the mass flow rate of the salt $\\Phi_m$ (kg/s).\n\n### 5.1. Physical Model\nSince there are no external torques acting on the vertical axis ($M_z \u003d 0$), the total [[Angular Momentum]] ($\\Gamma_z$) is conserved.\n$$ \\Gamma_{initial} \u003d \\Gamma_{final} $$\n\n### 5.2. Moment of Inertia Calculation\n*   **Initial Inertia ($J_1$):** Just the disc.\n    $$ J_{disk} \u003d \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 $$\n*   **Added Inertia ($J_{soli}$):** The salt forms a ring (or accumulates) at radius $b$.\n    The mass of the salt at time $t$ is $m_{soli}(t) \u003d \\Phi_m \\cdot t$.\n    Since it is at distance $b$ from the axis:\n    $$ J_{soli}(t) \u003d (\\Phi_m \\cdot t) \\cdot b^2 $$\n*   **Total Inertia at time $t$:**\n    $$ J_{tot}(t) \u003d \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 + \\Phi_m t b^2 $$\n\n### 5.3. Conservation Equation\n$$ J_{disk} \\omega_0 \u003d J_{tot}(t) \\omega(t) $$\n$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \\omega_0 \u003d \\left( \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 + \\Phi_m t b^2 \\right) \\omega(t) $$\n\n### 5.4. Solving for Mass Flow Rate ($\\Phi_m$)\nWe know at $t\u003d30$s, $\\omega(t) \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\omega_0$. Substituting this:\n\n$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \\omega_0 \u003d \\left( \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 + \\Phi_m t b^2 \\right) \\cdot \\frac{3}{4} \\omega_0 $$\n\nCancel $\\omega_0$:\n$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \u003d \\frac{3}{8} M R^2 + \\frac{3}{4} \\Phi_m t b^2 $$\n\nRearrange to find $\\Phi_m$:\n$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 - \\frac{3}{8} M R^2 \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\Phi_m t b^2 $$\n$$ \\frac{1}{8} M R^2 \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\Phi_m t b^2 $$\n\n$$ \\Phi_m \u003d \\frac{4 \\cdot M R^2}{8 \\cdot 3 \\cdot t \\cdot b^2} \u003d \\frac{M R^2}{6 t b^2} $$\n\n### 5.5. Numerical Calculation (Reverse Engineering Data)\nFrom the notes (Image 6), the following values are identified:\n*   $M \u003d 1 \\text{ kg}$\n*   $R \u003d 0.25 \\text{ m}$ (implied from $d\u003d2R$ or similar context)\n*   $t \u003d 30 \\text{ s}$\n*   $b$ (radius where salt falls) seems to be related to $R$, likely $b \\approx R$ or given separately.\n\nUsing the values from the bottom of Image 6:\n$$ \\Phi_m \u003d \\frac{1 \\cdot (0.25)^2}{6 \\cdot 30 \\cdot b^2} $$\n*(Note: The user notes derive $\\Phi_m \\approx 0.3 \\text{ kg/s}$, check input values for $b$ if explicitly stated in audio/text).*\n\n---\n\n## 6. Critical Analysis \u0026 Warning Notes\n\n### ⚠️ Warning: Reference Frames\nIn the collision problems (Section 3), be extremely careful about the **Reference Frame**. The equations $m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 \u003d \\dots$ are valid in the Lab frame. If calculating energy loss or scattering angles, converting to the **Center of Mass (CMS)** frame often simplifies the algebra, though the notes here brute-forced the trigonometry in the Lab frame.\n\n### ⚠️ Warning: Variable Mass Systems\nIn Section 5 (Salt on Disk), a common error is using $\\tau \u003d I \\alpha$. This form is strictly for constant moment of inertia. When mass changes, you **must** use the fundamental conservation law:\n$$ L \u003d \\text{const} \\implies I_1 \\omega_1 \u003d I_2 \\omega_2 $$\nDo not try to find angular acceleration $\\alpha$ and integrate; it is much harder and prone to error.\n\n### 💡 Justification of Method\nThe lecturer solved the \"Sila Curka\" (Jet Force) problem by integrating the force over time ($ \\int F dt$) conceptually to get the momentum change. This essentially averages the microscopic collisions of water molecules into a macroscopic continuous force $\\Phi_m v$. This is the standard Engineering/Fluid Dynamics control volume approach.",

        "text": ", separating general mechanics, fluid dynamics, and rotational dynamics.\n\n***\n\n# Lecture: Mechanics, Hydrodynamics \u0026 Rotational Dynamics\n\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "Date:** [[2025-11-27]]\n**Location:** Slovenia\n**Tags:** #"
      }, {
        "text": "Physics #Mechanics #Hydrodynamics #RotationalDynamics #Obsidian\n\n---\n\n## 1. General Formulas \u0026 Identities Used"
      }, {
        "text": "\nBefore diving into specific problems, the following mathematical identities and physical principles were utilized throughout the lecture:\n\n### Trigonometry"
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   **Fundamental Identity:** $\\sin^2 \\alpha + \\cos^2 \\alpha \u003d 1$\n*   **"
      }, {
        "text": "Cosine Rule (implied in vector subtraction):** $c^2 \u003d a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \\"
      }, {
        "text": "cos \\gamma$\n*   **Transformation:** Used to decouple coupled equations in elastic collisions.\n\n### Physics Principles\n*"
      }, {
        "text": "   **Newton\u0027s Second Law (Impulse form):** $\\vec{F} \u003d \\frac{d\\vec{G"
      }, {
        "text": "}}{dt} \\implies \\int \\vec{F} dt \u003d \\Delta \\vec{G}$\n*   "
      }, {
        "text": "**Conservation of Angular Momentum:** $\\Gamma_{total} \u003d \\text{const}$ if $M_{ext} \u003d 0$."
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   **Jet Force (Hydrodynamics):** $\\vec{F} \u003d \\Phi_m (\\vec{v}_{out} - \\vec"
      }, {
        "text": "{v}_{in})$ where $\\Phi_m \u003d \\rho S v$.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Linear"
      }, {
        "text": " Dynamics \u0026 Projectiles\n*(Based on Image 1)*\n\n### Problem Setup: Cylinder/Block Push\nA block of mass $m\u003d"
      }, {
        "text": "1 \\text{ kg}$ is pushed along a surface by a constant force $F\u003d500 \\text{ N}$"
      }, {
        "text": " for a distance $\\Delta x$ (related to diameter $2R\u003d10 \\text{ cm}$). It then behaves"
      }, {
        "text": " as a horizontal projectile falling from height $H\u003d10 \\text{ m}$.\n\n**Objective:** Calculate the range ("
      }, {
        "text": "domet) $d$.\n\n### 2.1. Acceleration Phase\nWe assume a constant force acts on the mass. Using"
      }, {
        "text": " [[Work-Energy Theorem]] or Kinematics:\n$$ F \u003d m \\cdot a \\implies a \u003d \\frac{F}{"
      }, {
        "text": "m} $$\nVelocity after pushing distance $\\Delta x$:\n$$ v^2 \u003d v_0^2 + 2a"
      }, {
        "text": " \\Delta x $$\nAssuming starting from rest ($v_0\u003d0$) and $\\Delta x \\approx 2R$"
      }, {
        "text": " (as per notes):\n$$ v \u003d \\sqrt{2 \\cdot \\frac{F}{m} \\cdot 2R"
      }, {
        "text": "} $$\n\n\u003e **Note to Self:** The notes define $\\Delta x \\le 2R$. The calculation assumes"
      }, {
        "text": " the force acts over the full diameter.\n\u003e *Calculation in notes:*\n\u003e $$ v \u003d \\sqrt{2 \\cdot \\"
      }, {
        "text": "frac{500}{1} \\cdot 0.1} \u003d \\sqrt{100} \u003d 10 \\text{"
      }, {
        "text": " m/s} $$\n\u003e *Wait, notes show $\\sqrt{300^2 \\dots}$. This segment"
      }, {
        "text": " connects to the \"bullet\" problem later. Let\u0027s stick to the visual derivation of the projectile part.*\n\n### 2.2."
      }, {
        "text": " Projectile Motion Phase\nOnce the object leaves the platform with horizontal velocity $v_x$, it falls height $H$.\nTime"
      }, {
        "text": " of flight $t$:\n$$ H \u003d \\frac{1}{2} g t^2 \\implies t \u003d \\sqrt"
      }, {
        "text": "{\\frac{2H}{g}} $$\nHorizontal range $d$:\n$$ d \u003d v_x \\cdot t \u003d v_x \\sqrt"
      }, {
        "text": "{\\frac{2H}{g}} $$\n\n### 2.3. Impulse \u0026 Average Force\nThe notes discuss the definition"
      }, {
        "text": " of external force as the time derivative of momentum ([[Impulse]]):\n$$ \\vec{F}_{zun} \u003d \\frac{d\\"
      }, {
        "text": "vec{G}}{dt} \\implies \\int \\vec{F} dt \u003d \\Delta \\vec{G} $$\n\n---\n\n## 3"
      }, {
        "text": ". Collisions in 2D\n*(Based on Image 2 and 3)*\n\n### Problem: Elastic/"
      }, {
        "text": "Inelastic Collision\nTwo bodies, masses $m_1$ and $m_2$, collide.\n*   **Initial State:** $m"
      }, {
        "text": "_1$ moves with $v_1$, $m_2$ is stationary ($v_2\u003d0$).\n*   **Final State"
      }, {
        "text": ":** They scatter at angles $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$.\n\n**Conservation of Momentum (Vectorial):**\n$$ m"
      }, {
        "text": "_1 \\vec{v}_1 \u003d m_1 \\vec{v}\u0027_1 + m_2 \\"
      }, {
        "text": "vec{v}\u0027_2 $$\n\n**Decomposition (x and y axes):**\n$$ X: \\quad m_1 v_1 \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " m_1 v\u0027_1 \\cos \\alpha + m_2 v\u0027_2 \\cos \\beta $$\n$$"
      }, {
        "text": " Y: \\quad 0 \u003d m_1 v\u0027_1 \\sin \\alpha - m_2 v\u0027_2"
      }, {
        "text": " \\sin \\beta $$\n\n### Critical Analysis: Solving the System\nThe lecturer performed a derivation to relate the angles."
      }, {
        "text": "\nFrom Y-direction:\n$$ v\u0027_1 \\sin \\alpha \u003d \\frac{m_2}{m_1} v\u0027_2 \\"
      }, {
        "text": "sin \\beta $$\nUsing the identity $\\sin^2 \\alpha + \\cos^2 \\alpha \u003d 1$, the"
      }, {
        "text": " notes derive a relationship between the cosine of the scattering angles, specifically resulting in:\n$$ \\cos \\alpha + 2 \\cos \\beta \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " 2 $$\n*(This specific result implies specific mass ratios or velocities were plugged in, e.g., $v"
      }, {
        "text": "_2 \u003d 2v_1$).*\n\n---\n\n## 4. Hydrodynamics: Force of a Jet"
      }, {
        "text": " (Sila Curka)\n*(Based on Image 4 and 5)*\n\n### Concept: Jet Impact\nA fluid jet with"
      }, {
        "text": " velocity $v$ and cross-section $S$ hits a plate. The force exerted is due to the change in momentum flux"
      }, {
        "text": ".\n\n$$ \\vec{F}_{curka} \u003d \\Phi_m (\\vec{v}_{out} - \\"
      }, {
        "text": "vec{v}_{in}) $$\nWhere mass flow rate $\\Phi_m \u003d \\rho S v$.\n\n###"
      }, {
        "text": " Problem: Jet Hitting a Hinged Plate\nA plate of mass $M$ and length $L$ hangs vertically"
      }, {
        "text": ". A jet hits it, deflecting it by angle $\\phi$.\n\n**Equilibrium of Moments:**\nTorque due"
      }, {
        "text": " to Gravity \u003d Torque due to Jet\n$$ M_g \u003d M_{curka} $$\n$$ m g \\frac{L}{2}"
      }, {
        "text": " \\sin \\phi \u003d F_{curka} \\cdot r_{curka} \\cdot \\cos \\phi $$\n*(Note"
      }, {
        "text": ": The cosine term comes from the component of the jet force perpendicular to the plate).*\n\n**Resulting Equation from Notes:**\n$$ \\sin"
      }, {
        "text": " \\phi \u003d \\frac{4 \\rho S v^2 h}{mg L} $$\nSolving for $\\phi$:\n$$ \\phi"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d \\arcsin \\left( \\frac{4 \\rho S v^2 h}{mg L} \\right"
      }, {
        "text": ") $$\n*Calculated result:* $\\phi \u003d 24.79^{\\circ}$.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Rot"
      }, {
        "text": "ational Dynamics: The \"Salt on Disk\" Problem\n*(Based on Image 5 and 6)*\n\n### Problem Statement\nWe"
      }, {
        "text": " have a rotating disc. Above it hangs a bag of salt.\n*   **Initial State:** Disc (radius $R$,"
      }, {
        "text": " mass $M$) rotates with $\\omega_0$. Bag is stationary above.\n*   **Process:** Salt falls uniformly"
      }, {
        "text": " from a hole in the bag onto the disc at a radius $b$.\n*   **System:** Disc + Accum"
      }, {
        "text": "ulating Salt.\n*   **Constraint:** After $t\u003d30$ seconds, the angular velocity drops to $\\omega(30)"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\omega_0$.\n\n**Objective:** Calculate the mass flow rate of the salt $\\"
      }, {
        "text": "Phi_m$ (kg/s).\n\n### 5.1. Physical Model\nSince there are no external torques acting on the vertical"
      }, {
        "text": " axis ($M_z \u003d 0$), the total [[Angular Momentum]] ($\\Gamma_z$) is conserved.\n"
      }, {
        "text": "$$ \\Gamma_{initial} \u003d \\Gamma_{final} $$\n\n### 5.2. Moment of Inertia Calculation"
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   **Initial Inertia ($J_1$):** Just the disc.\n    $$ J_{disk} \u003d \\frac{1}{"
      }, {
        "text": "2} M R^2 $$\n*   **Added Inertia ($J_{soli}$):** The salt forms"
      }, {
        "text": " a ring (or accumulates) at radius $b$.\n    The mass of the salt at time $t$ is $m_{"
      }, {
        "text": "soli}(t) \u003d \\Phi_m \\cdot t$.\n    Since it is at distance $b$"
      }, {
        "text": " from the axis:\n    $$ J_{soli}(t) \u003d (\\Phi_m \\cdot t) \\cdot b^2"
      }, {
        "text": " $$\n*   **Total Inertia at time $t$:**\n    $$ J_{tot}(t) \u003d \\frac{1"
      }, {
        "text": "}{2} M R^2 + \\Phi_m t b^2 $$\n\n### 5.3."
      }, {
        "text": " Conservation Equation\n$$ J_{disk} \\omega_0 \u003d J_{tot}(t) \\omega(t) $$\n$$ \\frac{"
      }, {
        "text": "1}{2} M R^2 \\omega_0 \u003d \\left( \\frac{1}{2} M"
      }, {
        "text": " R^2 + \\Phi_m t b^2 \\right) \\omega(t) $$\n\n### "
      }, {
        "text": "5.4. Solving for Mass Flow Rate ($\\Phi_m$)\nWe know at $t\u003d30$"
      }, {
        "text": "s, $\\omega(t) \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\omega_0$. Substituting this:\n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \\omega_0 \u003d \\left( \\frac{1"
      }, {
        "text": "}{2} M R^2 + \\Phi_m t b^2 \\right) \\cdot \\frac{3}{4} \\"
      }, {
        "text": "omega_0 $$\n\nCancel $\\omega_0$:\n$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003d \\frac{3}{8} M R^2 + \\frac{3}{4} \\Phi_m t b^2 $$"
      }, {
        "text": "\n\nRearrange to find $\\Phi_m$:\n$$ \\frac{1}{2} M R^2 - \\frac{3}{"
      }, {
        "text": "8} M R^2 \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\Phi_m t b^2 $$\n"
      }, {
        "text": "$$ \\frac{1}{8} M R^2 \u003d \\frac{3}{4} \\Phi_m"
      }, {
        "text": " t b^2 $$\n\n$$ \\Phi_m \u003d \\frac{4 \\cdot M R^2}{8 \\cdot 3"
      }, {
        "text": " \\cdot t \\cdot b^2} \u003d \\frac{M R^2}{6 t b^2} $$\n\n### 5."
      }, {
        "text": "5. Numerical Calculation (Reverse Engineering Data)\nFrom the notes (Image 6), the following values are identified:\n*   $M \u003d "
      }, {
        "text": "1 \\text{ kg}$\n*   $R \u003d 0.25 \\text{ m}$ (impl"
      }, {
        "text": "ied from $d\u003d2R$ or similar context)\n*   $t \u003d 30 \\text{ s}$\n"
      }, {
        "text": "*   $b$ (radius where salt falls) seems to be related to $R$, likely $b \\approx R$ or given"
      }, {
        "text": " separately.\n\nUsing the values from the bottom of Image 6:\n$$ \\Phi_m \u003d \\frac{1 \\cdot ("
      }, {
        "text": "0.25)^2}{6 \\cdot 30 \\cdot b^2} $$\n*(Note:"
      }, {
        "text": " The user notes derive $\\Phi_m \\approx 0.3 \\text{ kg/s}$, check input values for $b$ if"
      }, {
        "text": " explicitly stated in audio/text).*\n\n---\n\n## 6. Critical Analysis \u0026 Warning Notes\n\n### ⚠️ Warning: Reference"
      }, {
        "text": " Frames\nIn the collision problems (Section 3), be extremely careful about the **Reference Frame**. The equations $m_1 v_1 +"
      }, {
        "text": " m_2 v_2 \u003d \\dots$ are valid in the Lab frame. If calculating energy loss or scattering angles"
      }, {
        "text": ", converting to the **Center of Mass (CMS)** frame often simplifies the algebra, though the notes here brute-forced the trigonometry"
      }, {
        "text": " in the Lab frame.\n\n### ⚠️ Warning: Variable Mass Systems\nIn Section 5 (Salt on Disk), a"
      }, {
        "text": " common error is using $\\tau \u003d I \\alpha$. This form is strictly for constant moment of inertia. When mass changes, you"
      }, {
        "text": " **must** use the fundamental conservation law:\n$$ L \u003d \\text{const} \\implies I_1 \\omega_1 \u003d I"
      }, {
        "text": "_2 \\omega_2 $$\nDo not try to find angular acceleration $\\alpha$ and integrate; it is much"
      }, {
        "text": " harder and prone to error.\n\n### 💡 Justification of Method\nThe lecturer solved the \"Sila Curka\" ("
      }, {
        "text": "Jet Force) problem by integrating the force over time ($ \\int F dt$) conceptually to get the momentum change. This essentially"
      }, {
        "text": " averages the microscopic collisions of water molecules into a macroscopic continuous force $\\Phi_m v$. This is the standard Engineering/"
      }, {
        "text": "Fluid Dynamics control volume approach."
      }, {

      "text": "### Critical Analysis: The Mass Flow Rate ($\\Phi_m$) \u0026 Radius ($b$)\n\nThere is a crucial distinction to be made regarding the value $\\Phi_m \\approx 0.3 \\, \\text{kg/s}$ found in the notes.\n\n#### 1. Source of $\\Phi_m \u003d 0.3 \\, \\text{kg/s}$\nLooking closely at **Image 6 (Upper half)** and **Image 5 (Bottom half)**, the value $0.3 \\, \\text{kg/s}$ is calculated for the **Hydrodynamics (Jet)** problem, not originally for the Salt/Rotation problem.\n$$ \\Phi_m (\\text{jet}) \u003d \\rho \\cdot S \\cdot v $$\n$$ \\Phi_m \u003d 1000 \\, \\frac{\\text{kg}}{\\text{m}^3} \\cdot 10^{-4} \\, \\text{m}^2 \\cdot 3 \\, \\frac{\\text{m}}{\\text{s}} \u003d \\mathbf{0.3 \\, \\text{kg/s}} $$\n\n#### 2. Application to the Salt Problem (Problem 5)\nIf we assume the lecturer intended to reuse this mass flow rate ($\\Phi_m \u003d 0.3 \\, \\text{kg/s}$) for the bag of salt in the rotation problem, we can solve for the radius $b$ (where the salt falls).\n\n**The Derived Formula:**\nFrom the conservation of angular momentum derivation in Section 5.4:\n$$ \\Phi_m \u003d \\frac{M R^2}{6 t b^2} $$\n\n**Solving for $b$:**\n$$ b^2 \u003d \\frac{M R^2}{6 t \\Phi_m} \\implies b \u003d R \\sqrt{\\frac{M}{6 t \\Phi_m}} $$\n\n**Numerical Check:**\nAssuming standard parameters often reused in these lectures (e.g., $M\u003d1\\,\\text{kg}$) and using the time $t\u003d30\\,\\text{s}$:\n\n*   **Case A: Using $R\u003d0.25\\,\\text{m}$ (from Projectile problem context):**\n    $$ b \u003d 0.25 \\cdot \\sqrt{\\frac{1}{6 \\cdot 30 \\cdot 0.3}} \u003d 0.25 \\cdot \\sqrt{\\frac{1}{54}} \\approx 0.25 \\cdot 0.136 $$\n    $$ \\mathbf{b \\approx 0.034 \\, \\text{m} \u003d 3.4 \\, \\text{cm}} $$\n\n*   **Case B: Using $R\u003d0.05\\,\\text{m}$ (from Cylinder problem $2R\u003d10\\text{cm}$):**\n    $$ b \u003d 0.05 \\cdot \\sqrt{0.0185} \\approx 0.0068 \\, \\text{m} \u003d \\mathbf{0.68 \\, \\text{cm}} $$\n\n### **Conclusion**\nThe value $0.3 \\, \\text{kg/s}$ belongs to the water jet.
